Plant Overview

One interconnected mechanical ecosystem. The Reactor Core is the primary power source. Cooling is a closed-loop heat sink. Electrics distributes power through the switchboard. The Regulator is the central control station. Motors convert electrical power into propulsion. Fuel and auxiliary diesels provide backup. Every component affects the others — a cooling failure raises temperatures, derates the generator, stresses the bus, and eventually starves the motors. After any critical event the Engineering Terminal is the final recovery step.

Dependency chain

  1. Reactor / Generator produces electrical power (fuel + air, heat-limited)
  2. Cooling closed-loop removes heat — failure raises temps plant-wide
  3. Electrics distributes power via main switchboard & breakers
  4. Regulator monitors and sets demand / throttle
  5. Motors convert available power into RPM, torque and ship speed
  6. Aux diesels + fuel system supply limited backup when primary is derated
  7. Any crisis → stabilise systems → Engineering Terminal is last required action

Sector A — Electrics 3★

How it works

Main breaker closes the bus. Motor 1 and Motor 2 are alternate propulsion feeds. Use ONE feed for ~50–60s then switch to the other to reset unit heat. BOTH feeds give max speed but heat rises fast. Starter/Aux are house loads.

Connected to: Reactor (power in) → Motors & Aux (power out). Panel heat rises with current.

Close the main breaker and feed the loads. Power comes from the Reactor. P = V × I.

Sector B — Cooling 4★

How it works

Lubricant and seawater pumps circulate coolant through the coolers. This is the plant heat sink — there is no cooling heat meter. Keep pumps on when the reactor or motors are loaded.

Connected to: Absorbs heat from Reactor & Motors; stabilises bulk temperature and helps unit heat fall.

Sector C — Reactor Core 5★

How it works

Generator converts fuel/air energy into electrical power (P = V × I on the bus). Balance fuel feed and air intake. High output without cooling drives reactor unit heat and plant temperature.

Connected to: Fuel system → Electrics bus → whole plant. Efficiency drops when overheated.

Fuel + Air → Heat → Dynamo → Generator. ṁf = Pe / (ηt × ηg × F.E.ρ)

Sector D — Regulator 1★

How it works

Throttle sets how hard the ship asks for propulsion. Auto-regulate can track available power. Sustained high throttle heats the regulator path.

Connected to: Demand signal toward Motors; depends on Electrics power and fuel availability.

Throttle sets demand and couples to ship speed. ṁf = ρ(T) × Q

Sector E — Back Motors 2★

How it works

Clutch couples the shaft to the bus-powered motors. RPM tracks your target when power and heat allow — up to 1200. Low RPM holds mild stable heat; high RPM climbs fast. Props stop if the bus dies or clutch opens.

Connected to: Electrics (bus power) → shaft → ship speed. Cooling limits heat rise.

Clutch in and set target RPM. ω = 2πN/60   P = T × ω. Needs bus power from Electrics.
